newsitem.title: UK: Copper prices slacken, but oil builds on gains.
newsitem.headline: Copper prices slacken, but oil builds on gains.

text.p: Copper prices drifted lower on Thursday in a market unsettled by expectations of an increase in London Metal Exchange (LME) stocks.
But world oil prices extended recent gains as cold weather and refinery strikes in France bit into supplies of refined products amid robust consumer demand, traders said.
LME copper finished at the day's lows below the $2,200 support level after veering lower during late LME trading.
Attention was being focused on Friday's stocks data, and the market was anticipating another build in stocks after months of steady declines.
Traders said that copper is still in the grip of a major battle between strong players on both sides of the market, which was likely to continue in the short-term.
A shift beyond either side of the recent price range could spark savage price movements, traders added.
Gold prices, which had bounced from three-year lows on Wednesday, came under renewed pressure in early European business as rumours intensified that a central bank was selling some of its reserves.
European central banks are believed to be looking at their reserves as a potential source of funding to help their governments meet the economic criteria necessary for European Monetary Union.
"There are a lot of guessing games going on at the moment," said bullion analyst Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland.
But prices crept higher after the attempt to sell the market lower was beaten off, and ended just firmer at $370.00 an ounce.
In the oil market, international marker crude Brent Blend traded at its contract high of $24.25 a barrel, a 47 cent rise on the day, before easing back slightly in the afternoon.

Oil prices have been consolidating at higher levels despite the prospect of imminent Iraqi oil sales because of strong demand in a fairly balanced market vulnerable to any potential supply disruption.
Chicago Board of Trade wheat prices were slightly firmer at $3.80-1/2, up 2-1/4 cents, towards mid-session.
Sugar continued recovering from a fierce bout of selling earlier in the week, but failed to push through the psychological $300 barrier in London.
London cocoa prices surged higher in a late rally driven by speculative buying.
But coffee prices dipped to a new low.
